evals.name: no-corrections
evals.setup: A finished conversation. The user ran `/craft:cm` once; the skill read the staged diff and produced a commit message the user accepted without change ("perfect, thanks"). Nothing else was corrected, retried, or walked back. `craft/skills/cm/SKILL.md` is a writable checkout, already carries the `## Self-learning` block, and has no sibling `LESSONS.md`.

evals.name: correction-generalized
evals.setup: The user ran `/go:review` on a package. The review called a `defer rows.Close()` inside a loop a style nit; the user pushed back: "that's not a nit, it's a real leak — the file handle lives until the function returns. Flag resource leaks as bugs, not style." The agent agreed and re-filed it. `go/skills/review/` is a writable checkout with the `## Self-learning` block and no sibling `LESSONS.md`.

evals.name: attribute-to-the-driving-skill
evals.setup: A session correcting two skills. `craft:cm` was told to derive the commit type from the diff rather than the branch name. `srd:create` was told that Lifecycle values are written uppercase after it wrote one lowercase — a rule the SRD standard it fetches live already carries as LIF-1 (the frozen eval copy is `srd/evals/mocks/srd/fixtures/srd-standard.md`), and which `srd:create`'s own body already follows. A third correction, about running `git push`, belongs to no skill in the session.

evals.name: single-skill-harvest
evals.setup: A session correcting two skills. `go:review` was told that a `defer rows.Close()` inside a loop is a resource leak to flag as a bug, not a style nit. `craft:cm` was then told to derive the commit type from the diff rather than the branch name. Both `go/skills/review/` and `craft/skills/cm/` are writable checkouts with the `## Self-learning` block and no sibling `LESSONS.md`.
